Theme

holy water noun

also blessed water

medieval

M-O s.v. holy water, after Du Cange and Marco Polo (c. 1300)

aqua benedicta

Water blessed by a priest, from benedīcere. The West keeps it in a stoup by the church door for the sign of the cross; the East blesses water solemnly at Theophany, and the faithful drink it and sprinkle their houses with it.

Other words

  • aqua sāncta

    also used · late Latin · Vulg. Num. 5.17: assūmetque aquam sānctam in vāse fictilī

    The Vulgate’s phrase, of the holy water of the Law.

  • aqua lustrālis — lustral water, for pagan purification

    also used · classical · Ov. Pont. 3.2.73 (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short translate Ovid’s phrase “holy water”; it is the water of pagan rites.

Examples

  • Sacerdōs domum aquā benedictā aspergit.

    The priest is sprinkling the house with holy water.composed

See also priest, church.

SourcesLewis & Short: aqua · Lewis & Short: benedico · Lewis & Short: lustralis
